Nb-Containing Medium-Mn Low-Density Steels
Chen Ma, Jianlei Zhang,* Fenghui An, Gang Chen, Junye Zhou, Changjiang Song,
and Qijie Zhai
Microalloying of Nb has been commonly utilized to enhance the structure and
mechanical properties of advanced high-strength steel (AHSS), but its application
in medium-Mn low-density steel has been relatively understudied. This study
aims to investigate the evolution of nano-scale precipitates and mechanical
properties of Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C-0.02/0.04Nb low-density steels. The findings
reveal that the austenite grain size of 0.04Nb steels is approximately half that of
0.02Nb steels due to the precipitation of NbC particles. Moreover, the addition of
Nb is found to elevate the formation energy of κ-carbide, thereby impeding its
growth and coarsening. Consequently, the intragranular κ-carbides in 0.04Nb
steels are consistently smaller than those in 0.02Nb steels, with no coarsened
intergranular κ-carbides detected in either steel variant after aging treatment
at 723–823 K. Despite a slight reduction on precipitation strengthening of
κ-carbides with higher Nb content, the yield strength of 0.04Nb steels exceeds that
of 0.02Nb steels by ≈71 MPa, mainly due to additional fine grain strengthening and
dislocation strengthening. The strengthening mechanisms in the Nb-containing
low-density steels are analyzed quantitatively. The role of Nb in regulating the
microstructure and mechanical properties of medium-Mn low-density steels is
comprehensively discussed, offering valuable insights for the alloy design of low-
density steel.

κ-carbides in medium-Mn low-density steels appears to be more
challenging. The higher Mn content in steels could slow down

The addition of microalloying elements, such as Ti, V, and Nb,
has been shown to effectively control the microstructure and
performance of medium-Mn steel.<sup>[18–20]</sup> A study by Park et al.
demonstrated that the addition of 0.2 wt% V could trigger the
formation of VC precipitates in a Fe-8Mn-0.2C-3Al (wt%) steel,
leading to significant grain refinement in austenite and a
strength enhancement of 246 MPa.<sup>[18]</sup> Similar effects on grain
refinement and strength enhancement also observed in
Ti-containing and Nb-containing medium-Mn steels, due to
the formation of TiC and NbC particles.<sup>[19,20]</sup> The addition of
0.05 wt% Nb to a Fe-5.6Mn-1.2Al-0.17C steel could refine the
austenite grain by forming nano-scale Nb(C, N) particles.<sup>[20]</sup>
Additionally, the smaller average austenite grain caused by the
precipitation of Nb(C, N) particles was proven to improve the
stability of austenite.<sup>[20]</sup> However, there are few research on
how microalloying elements regulate the microstructure and per-
formance of medium-Mn low-density steels, especially for the
precipitation behaviors of κ-carbides.
Park et al. have reported that the addition of 0.1 wt% Nb
resulted in the formation of NbC carbides in a Fe-20Mn-8Al
1.0C (wt%) steel, which reduced the C content in austenite,
decreasing the precipitation of κ-carbides.<sup>[21]</sup> The Nb(C, N)
carbides typically possess a hard characteristic, contributing to
significant strain-hardening potential.<sup>[22]</sup> But it was questionable
whether the limited formation of NbC could significantly reduce
the C content in austenite and thus affect the formation of
κ-carbides. Consequently, the influence of Nb microalloying
on the microstructure and mechanical properties of medium-Mn
low-density steel is worth exploring in detail. This work designed
two Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C-0.02/0.04Nb (wt%) low-density steels
to explore the microstructural evolution and mechanical proper-
ties of the Nb-containing medium-Mn low-density steels.
Considering the influence of aging treatment on the nano-
precipitation behavior in low-density steels, especially
κ-carbides,<sup>[8,23]</sup> the studied steels were further aged at 723,
773, and 823 K. The microstructure evolution was examined
using a scanning electron microscope (SEM) equipped with elec-
tron back scatter diffraction (EBSD) system and a transmission
electron microscope (TEM). Additionally, the influence of Nb
addition on the nano-precipitation behavior was elucidated
through thermodynamic calculations and first-principle
calculations.
2. Experimental Section
The Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C (wt%) low-density steels with
0.02 wt% and 0.04 wt% Nb addition in this work were prepared
using a centrifugal casting method under near-rapid solidifica-
tion. Initially, the ingot was prepared by induction melting in
a water-cooled copper crucible. Subsequently, the ingot was
re-melted and swiftly poured into a rotating copper mold
at a high speed to obtain steel strips with dimensions of
6 0 \times 7 0 \times 2 . 5
mm through near-rapid solidification. Aging treat-
ment was performed on a portion of these steel strips in a tubular
vacuum furnace at temperatures of 723, 773, and 823 K for 3 h.
Subsequently, an appropriate aging temperature was selected to
investigate the structure evolution and mechanical properties of
steels under different aging periods. For simplicity, hereafter, the
steels containing 0.02 wt% Nb and 0.04 wt% Nb are referred to as
0.02Nb steels and 0.04Nb steels, respectively.
The actual measured chemical compositions of steel strips are
presented in . X-ray diffraction (XRD) analysis for the
steel strips was conducted using a D/max-2500 instrument at
40 kV, scanning in the range of 30°–100° with a speed of
4°/min. An Apollo 300 thermal field emission SEM equipped
with an EBSD detector was used for the microstructure charac-
terization. The scanning step size for EBSD characterization was
set as 300 nm. Prior to SEM observation, the samples underwent
electropolishing with 10 vol% perchloric acid alcohol solution
under 25 V for a duration of 10 s. To analyze the elemental dis-
tribution, an electron probe microanalysis (EPMA) was carried
out using a JXA-8050G instrument at an electron beam voltage
of 15 kV. The TEM characterization for the nano-scale precipi
tates was conducted using a JEOL JEM-2100 TEM operating at
200 kV. For the preparation of TEM specimen, a double-jet elec-
tropolishing technique was utilized with a solution composed of
10% perchloric acid and 90% alcohol acid at a temperature of
≈ 30 °C and a voltage of 35 V. The microhardness of the strips
was measured using a Vickers hardness tester (MH-5L) with an
indentation load of 200 gf and a holding time of 20 s. The tensile
property tests were carried out using a MTS Criterion 44 univer-
sal testing machine at ambient temperature. The strain rate dur-
ing the tests was set as
. The test specimens had a
gauge width of 4 mm and a gauge length of 12 mm to ensure
consistent measurements. To ensure accurate data analysis, each
steel strip underwent a minimum of four repetitions during the
testing process.
To explore the influence of Nb addition on the formation of
κ-carbide, this study employed spin-polarized density functional
theory (DFT) calculations within the generalized gradient approx-
imation (GGA) utilizing the first-principles Perdew–Burke–
Ernzerhof (PBE) recipe, which was implemented in Vienna
Ab Initio Simulation Package (VASP).<sup>[24–27]</sup> The ion nuclei were
characterized by projected enhanced wave (PAW) potentials,<sup>[28,29]</sup>
while the valence electrons were treated with a plane-wave basis
set and a kinetic energy cutoff of 500 eV. To accurately compen-
sate for the partial occupation of the Kohn–Sham orbitals, the
Gaussian smearing approach was utilized with a width of
0.05 eV. The convergence of the geometry optimization process
was determined by ensuring that the energy change was below
0.03 eV Å<sup>1</sup>. The U scheme with a value of 2.59 eV was applied
for Fe atoms. The slab structure had a vacuum spacing of 15 Å in
the direction perpendicular to the structure plane. Brillouin zone
integration of the structure was achieved using
6 \times 6 \times 6
Monkhorst–Pack k-point sampling.

Density Steels
The uniaxial tensile tests reveal that enhancing Nb content and
employing aging treatment could increase the yield strength, as
evidenced by Figure 9 and Table 2. As the austenite accounts for
over 80 vol% volume fraction, it plays a dominant role in deter-
mining the mechanical properties of low-density steels.
Consequently, a quantitative analysis is carried out to assess

spans.content: 5. Conclusions
This study investigated the effects of Nb content on microstruc-
ture evolution and mechanical properties of the medium-Mn
Fe-12Mn-9Al-3Cr-1.4C-0.02/0.04Nb (wt%) low-density steels.
The following are the main findings that can be summarized:
1) Both the 0.02Nb and 0.04Nb steels consisted of ferrite and
austenite, with a ferrite content of ≈16 vol%. The increase of
Nb content promoted the formation of NbC particles, thereby
refining the austenite grain size significantly. 2) The Nb element
was found to be detrimental to the formation and growth of
κ-carbides, which was attributed to the increased formation
energy of κ-carbide by Nb doping. Because of this, the aging treat-
ment at 723–823 K could significantly promote the growth of
κ-carbides in Nb-containing steels, but no coarsened intergranu-
lar κ-carbides were observed. 3) Compared to the 0.02Nb steels,
the addition of 0.04 wt% Nb resulted in the yield strength
improvement of ≈71 MPa. Based on the strengthening mecha-
nism analysis, the increase in Nb content enhanced the disloca-
tion strengthening and grain refinement strengthening, while it
also reduced the κ-carbide content in the austenite, thereby weak-
ening the precipitation strengthening effect in the steels. 4) With
increasing the aging temperature, the dislocation density in
the Nb-containing low-density steels decreased, weakening the
dislocation strengthening, but the precipitation and growth of
κ-carbides enhanced the precipitation strengthening in the steel
significantly. For the Nb-containing steels aged at temperatures
exceeding 773 K, the precipitation of κ-carbide was the principal
strengthening factor.
